correctness.rationale: The theorem uses genuine fixed points of geometric realization, with barycentric weights constant on H-orbits, not just vertexwise fixed simplices. The orbit incompatibility graph exactly represents admissible fixed simplex supports. For rotation r^d, the orbits are residue classes modulo d; if d divides n they contain antipodal chord edges and all are forbidden. Otherwise d|2n forces d=2m, n congruent m mod d, giving the quotient Möbius graph M_2m (including M2=K2). Adjoining a reflection reduces to i->b-i on this quotient. Even b yields an m/2-centred pair of ladder rails with t=ceil(m/2) rungs; odd b deletes its two rim-edge orbits and, if needed, an antipodal one, giving t=max(0,floor(m/2)-1). Neighborhood-folds N(a1) subset N(b2) and then N(b1) subset N(a2) reduce Ind(L_t) to suspension of Ind(L_(t-2)), with L1 and L2 both S0, yielding S^floor((t-1)/2). Independent orbit enumeration directly tested all divisors d and reflection cosets for 4<=n<=40 and found the specified empty/Möbius/ladder graphs, including edge parity and small cutoffs. The Smith equality criterion uses Agarwal–Basak’s source theorem: ambient total mod-two Betti 4 when n≡2 mod4, 2 otherwise, whereas both reflection fixed spheres have total Betti 2; hence equality iff n not ≡2 mod4. Finite tests are corroboration, not an all-size proof.
